visual_logic: Isolates a single flanged leaf tooth to showcase the small, structurally distinct herbivorous dental profile of heavily armored thyreophorans, differentiating it from the massive blocks of ceratopsians.
prompt: High-fidelity 3D asset render of a single fossilized tooth from an Ankylosaurus, capturing its signature small, leaf-shaped crown morphology in a 3D animated feature film aesthetic. The tooth features a prominent, sharp vertical ridge running down the center of the crown face, flanked by distinct, prominent flanged serrations (cusplets) along the margins, giving it a stylized leaf or hand-fan silhouette. The fossil surface has a dark, highly mineralized brown and charcoal patina with a clean, low-gloss matte finish that highlights the structural ridges. The single tooth is isolated and oriented vertically, centered perfectly on a 1:1 square canvas. Rendered with soft studio lighting and precise ambient occlusion to maximize surface detail. The background is a seamless, solid light-grey studio plane that extends to the image edges with no internal frames, borders, or boxes. The object is scaled to preserve a strict 25% empty background safety margin on all four sides to prevent UI clipping. Grounded flat with realistic contact shadows. A clean checkered black-and-white scientific scale bar sits centered at the bottom.
